notes: 2026-02-18 discovery call (Jordan/Priya) - strong interest in low-latency streaming for inline completions in VS Code extension.
Customer profile: VS Code extension publisher with ~120 employees; main product distributes a copilot to enterprise customers (SaaS + self-hosted installs).
Primary ask: sub-100ms median response for inline suggestions (single-line completions) and <200ms for multi-line streaming; aim to feel 'native' inside editor.
Traffic/scale: target POC load = 200 concurrent active devs, peak RPS ~1,200 for completion endpoints, average tokens per completion ~18 tokens.
Cost sensitivity: high. Wants predictable unit economics; open to reserved capacity if it reduces per-token cost for high-traffic customers.

Model constraints: want model/version pinning per workspace and per-customer; support for lightweight 4-bit quantized variants for edge customers; fallback chain to smaller models when latency impacted.
Routing needs: region-aware routing (EU residency for some enterprise customers), canaries for model rollouts, and automatic fallback policy if head model overloaded.
Auth & tenancy: extension uses org-installed API keys and per-user tokens; require SSO/SAML through customer identity provider plus optional per-org API key managed in Redwood Console.
Rate limiting: need per-org and per-user quotas, burst handling in extension (client-side throttling) and server-side enforcement; want rate-limit headers for extension UX.
Telemetry/observability: need token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and sampling for reproduction of hallucination cases (logs tied to workspace id), 90d retention for traces.
Security review: sent initial security questionnaire 2026-02-20 (drive link). They flagged audit logs, KMS key rotation, and data retention as must-haves.

POC plan agreed: 4-week technical POC. Week1: integration + streaming demo; Week2: latency tuning (batching off for inline), Week3: scale test + fallback behavior, Week4: security checklist + runbook handoff.
Technical concerns raised on call: client-side websocket vs server-sent events for streaming inside VS Code extension; extension will prefer binary websocket stream for lower overhead.
Quote from Kepler CTO: 'If we can hit native feel within the editor, we'll roll Redwood across the paid tiers. Cost needs to be predictable.'

Legal/security: procurement wants SOC2 + contractual clause for data residency for certain EU customers; asked for a template DPA and KMS integration notes.
Integration tasks: extension auth flow (exchange client token -> short-lived inference token), SDK wrapper for streaming responses, per-workspace model pinning UI in Extension settings.
Jira: raised INFRA-4127 for per-tenant rate-limit headers + backoff hooks; customer will test backoff UX in 2nd week of POC.
Next tactical: Jordan to send SOW draft (template) and add Kepler to Dedicated pilot queue if legal greenlights; Priya to own POC runbook.
